A fun, but very limited time killer.  As other reviewers have stated, the matchmaking is slow but once you get into one it has that really enjoyable element of chaos that I love in a 'Hoard' mode.  The ability to change character classes, upgrade weapons and change perks adds a bit of a 'level up' element to the game, but everything you get seems to be more of a horizontal shift, (i.e. improve accuracy but reduce handling).  There is really no piece of equipment that is better than another so you dont save up to buy or work on winning anything.  If this had a larger amount of weapon upgrades that were scaled so they get better it would greatly increase replay ability IMO.   A more impactful 'skill tree' would also be a welcome addition.  

It's a ton of fun but a few additions could really have made this game a powerhouse.  Still great to play if you dont pay too much for it.

[h3]More Xenos than a Space Exterminator's Nightmare![/h3]

Oh, boy, strap on your pulse rifles and shine those flamethrowers, because Aliens: Fireteam Elite is the intergalactic rollercoaster I never knew I needed! It's like the aliens looked at my wish list and said, "Sure, let's give this human a chance to be a xenomorph exterminator with a pulse rifle in hand!"

First off, the graphics are so sharp, I can practically see the fear in those acid-drooling Xenomorph eyes. The attention to detail is so good that I wouldn't be surprised if I found Ripley's signature on one of the ammo crates.

The teamwork aspect is both a blessing and a hilarious disaster waiting to happen. I've never seen so many people panic and start blasting wildly when the Alien Queen makes her grand entrance. It's like a chaotic dance of bullets and screams, and I love every second of it. Forget trust falls; surviving a Xenomorph onslaught with your teammates is the ultimate team-building exercise.

The variety of weapons is like a buffet for a gun enthusiast. Pulse rifles, flamethrowers, smartguns – it's like a space arsenal dream come true. I'm pretty sure I heard my character shout, "Get away from her, you buggers!" at one point, and I couldn't stop laughing. It's the kind of cheesy line that makes you appreciate the game even more.

And let's talk about those Xenomorphs – they're like the party crashers you didn't invite but can't help but admire for their dedication to mayhem. The way they crawl on walls and ceilings is like a horror movie come to life. It's so immersive that I found myself checking my ceiling for facehuggers after a particularly intense gaming session.

In conclusion, Aliens: Fireteam Elite is not just a game; it's a therapy session for anyone who ever yelled at the screen during an Alien movie, saying, "I could do better than that!" Get ready to unleash your inner Ripley, laugh in the face of danger, and remember: in space, no one can hear you scream... unless it's over voice chat. Happy Xenomorph hunting!
They do indeed come outta the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ walls!
Shoot Aliens, see the 80's retro-future, cry that their lives belong to corporations just like ours. 10/10
